answer: Operator-Linked Escrow Quotas. Each new identity must post escrow through a payment rail tied to the operator's real account, recorded in an atlas of operator-to-identity edges. Escrow releases only after the identity completes a delta of validated work over several epochs. If any identity linked to an operator is caught sybiling, every sibling identity's escrow is forfeited and the operator's future quota is cut, so the comet of new wallets costs the operator real capital per identity rather than per wallet.
